## 固定收益開篇主論

8月14日美債一度因數據疲弱而上漲，但隨油價再度走高、美國可能加大對伊朗施壓，市場重新要求通膨補償，長端也持續承受財政供給壓力，漲勢因而逆轉。7月零售銷售下降0.6%，創一年多來最大跌幅；8月消費者信心初值降至51，低於市場共識的55。數據一度將2年期殖利率壓至4.10%以下，也促使交易員降低對聯準會9月升息的預期，但截至完整收盤，各期限殖利率均告上升。

2年期殖利率上升2.8個基點至4.171%，5年期上升4.8個基點至4.365%，10年期上升4.9個基點至4.693%，30年期則上升4.6個基點至5.261%。2年與10年期利差擴大2.1個基點至52.2個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大1.8個基點至109個基點。這反映近期升息風險下降，卻未減少投資人對較長期限債券所要求的補償；當日行情也不只是前端上漲，能源與通膨定價的逆轉幅度，足以讓政策敏感型殖利率在收盤時同樣走高。

10年期名目殖利率的漲幅幾乎由實質利率和預期通膨各占一半：10年期實質殖利率上升2.5個基點至2.41%，10年期損益兩平通膨率增加2.4個基點至2.283%。這項組成呈現當日兩股相互拉扯的訊號。消費支出轉弱，降低了內需本身迫使聯準會立即行動的機率，卻未消除赤字、龐大公私部門借款所帶來的實質融資壓力，也未排除新一波能源衝擊打斷近期通膨改善的可能。

油價是行情逆轉的關鍵。美國財政部長Scott Bessent承諾下週對伊朗採取更多經濟措施，美國同時維持對伊朗港口的封鎖，WTI因而上漲1.42%至$82.40，布蘭特原油上漲1.67%至$88.52，後者全週累計漲幅接近6%。7月消費者與生產者通膨原本受惠於能源成本下降，因此局勢升高格外重要。週五油價上漲並未改寫已公布的數據，卻提高了能源對通膨的有利貢獻僅屬暫時的風險。

整體市場表現為審慎，而非失序逃離風險。標普500指數下跌0.17%，那斯達克100指數下跌0.13%，費城半導體指數下跌0.31%；美元指數走弱0.29%，黃金期貨則上漲0.39%至$4,380.40。長天期資產受創最明顯：20年期以上美債指數下跌0.71%，長天期投資級公司債指數跌幅約四分之三個百分點。這些跌幅既反映其對基準公債利率變動的長存續期間曝險，也顯示初級市場環境更為嚴苛。

因此，當日行情是寬慰情緒消退，而非市場否定疲弱數據。經歷就業轉弱、消費者與生產者通膨溫和，以及週五支出下降的一週後，交易員持續撤除9月升息部位。芝加哥聯準銀行總裁Austan Goolsbee也承認，過去3個月的通膨數據已更令人鼓舞；但他仍希望再看到3至4個月類似6月的表現，才會相信通膨正重返2%。與此同時，油價、美債供給及日益廣泛的AI相關融資需求，繼續將長期借款成本維持在高檔。

## 消費轉弱，但油價重掌利率敘事

經歷較強勁的上半年後，7月零售報告顯示動能明顯流失。銷售額下降0.6%，其中非實體店面零售商下滑2.2%，汽車與零件經銷商減少1.8%；13個類別中有5個下降。報告中唯一的服務類別餐廳與酒吧成長0.5%，因此數據尚不足以證明消費全面疲弱，但跌勢的廣度及集中程度，已足以引發市場對非必需性需求的疑慮。

部分逆轉可能來自日曆效應。Amazon將Prime Day由一年前的7月提前至6月，使部分網購支出移至前一個月。這是解讀非實體店面銷售下降2.2%時的重要條件，卻不能抹去汽車銷售同步下滑及信心惡化的事實。密西根大學8月消費者信心初值降至51，比預測中位數低4點；即使最新通膨數據已有改善，家庭信心仍顯著轉弱。

消費者的財務緩衝也已變薄。6月個人儲蓄率為2.7%，不到兩年前的一半，並接近1947年以來資料區間的低端。近期通膨年增率曾超過平均時薪增幅，使部分家庭能夠存下的金額減少。股市財富增加支撐了資產持有者的消費，但若家庭不舉債或出售資產，消費持續成長不可能無限期依靠儲蓄率下降。

在這樣的背景下，7月銷售下降比單一月份的疲弱數字更具意義。由於一項大型促銷活動移至6月，數據並不能證明經濟已陷入衰退或消費將持續萎縮，卻顯示家庭若再遭遇一輪能源或商品價格壓力，可在不削減其他支出的情況下承受衝擊的空間已更有限。債市最初的反應正反映這項風險：短期美債上漲，2年期殖利率一度降至6月30日以來最低。

利率合約顯示，投資人同時撤除9月升息押注，以及截至2027年年中升息超過一次的預期。市場一度僅反映9月約8個基點的緊縮幅度，低於7月31日的近19個基點。這波重新定價始於8月7日公布的疲弱7月就業數據，並在溫和的消費者與生產者通膨數據出爐後加速。

Goolsbee的談話支持耐心觀望，卻不認同通膨問題已經解決。他支持7月會議維持利率不變，並形容經濟成長與勞動市場大致穩定。經歷5至6個月不利數據後，通膨仍是他的首要疑慮，但他認為過去3個月的表現令人鼓舞，可能顯示關稅與油價衝擊正在逐步消退。

他對提高信心設定了嚴格條件：還要再有3至4個月類似6月的數據。Goolsbee強調，通膨高於目標已超過5年，而過往高通膨一旦形成，扭轉過程往往困難且代價高昂。他也表示，若零售銷售連續數月下降，將令他感到不安；這為經濟成長保留了另一項判斷門檻，而不是將單月疲弱報告視為決定性證據。

7月會議已顯示較鷹派的陣營正在形成，3名政策官員當時主張升息25個基點而投下反對票。週五數據削弱其他官員立即加入該陣營的理由，但Goolsbee的立場並非主張寬鬆，而是應等待足夠時間，確認近期通膨降溫是否兼具廣度與持續性，同時觀察招聘與支出轉弱會不會演變成更嚴重的需求放緩。

油價使這項等待主張未能轉化為持久的美債漲勢。Bessent表示，美國將在下週宣布旨在加強伊朗經濟孤立的措施，並繼續封鎖伊朗港口。布蘭特原油週五盤中一度在$87附近交易，最後收於$88.52。市場注意力因此由已公布的7月通膨，轉回限制伊朗貿易可能如何影響未來數據中的能源成本。

隨後的債市賣壓並不限於損益兩平通膨率。實質殖利率走高，顯示在融資需求龐大之際，投資人持有長天期債券也要求更多補償。最近完成的$250億、30年期美債標售以5.216%得標，是2001年以來同類標售最高借款利率；至週五收盤，30年期殖利率又比該水準高出4.5個基點。標售需求尚稱充足，投標倍數為2.39倍，接近近期平均，但這表示投資人願意在高殖利率下承接，而非願意以顯著較低的殖利率吸收長天期債券。

不同期限的表現仍清楚呈現這項差異。2年期殖利率全週下降2.5個基點，10年期上升4.7個基點，30年期則上升5.9個基點。以一個月計，30年期殖利率上升15.5個基點，2年期卻下降2.4個基點。近期聯準會升息預期轉弱，但財政供給、能源不確定性及資金競爭持續推動殖利率曲線陡峭化。

## 發債潮後，信用債買方開始反制

對補償的要求在美國投資級債市場表現得更為明確。發行人壓低最終定價後，投資人於一週內撤回約36%的高評級債券初始訂單，訂單流失率是前一週的兩倍，也遠高於今年22%的平均水準。週四流失率達45%，創2026年最高紀錄。

Advanced Micro Devices是最鮮明的例子。公司縮減借款利差後，其$47.5億發債案中最長期限券別的訂單減少逾半。債券最終仍順利配售，投資級信用債的整體需求也保持穩健，但投資人已表明，龐大的帳面訂單並不代表願意接受任何定價。

此前兩週發行量達$1,360億，使8月可能成為歷來發行最繁忙的8月。企業為收購、再融資及AI基礎設施建設而舉債，在美債殖利率接近多年高點之際增加公司債的利率風險供給。承銷商預期下一週供給將放緩至約$200億，讓投資人在密集發行期後稍作喘息。

若以較長期歷史標準衡量，企業融資環境依然有利。投資級債平均利差約比美債高0.78個百分點，投資這類債券的基金截至週三當週吸引近$30億資金流入。改變的是邊際議價能力：投資人仍願意提供資金，但借款人試圖再壓低最後幾個基點的定價時，買方已較不願維持原先膨脹的訂單規模。

Zenith Arc發行$22.5億綠色債券，反映投資級市場以外的融資既可取得、代價也不低。這家由Fluidstack與Next Frontier成立的合資企業，以每1美元面額99.5美分為5年期債券定價，殖利率接近9%，位於先前討論區間的寬端。穆迪給予該債務Ba2評級，低於投資級兩個級距。

資金將用於在奧克拉荷馬州中部興建資料中心及變電站，並出租給Jane Street旗下子公司。15年期三重淨租賃除基本租金外，也由承租人負擔營運成本、稅款、公用事業費、保險及電力費用，另有Jane Street Group提供慣常擔保。這些合約付款為債權人提供明確現金流來源，但債券以討論區間寬端定價，顯示投資人仍要求相當高的補償，以承擔建設、技術及單一專案曝險。

這筆交易也擴大綠色融資在資料中心建設上的運用。此類專案的永續債券銷售額由2024年的$76億增至2025年的$112億，Edged Compute與TeraWulf也已分別籌得$13億及$32億。環境標章擴大了潛在投資人群體，卻未使買方忽視槓桿或專案風險。

Kedrion Biopharma擬議的€20億融資，則顯示資金充裕的貸款機構正考慮槓桿的另一種用途。這家血漿製品公司正與私募信貸業者洽談借款，部分資金可能用於向Permira及阿布達比投資局等股東發放股利。交易仍在評估，尚未達成協議；若完成，將把併購市場低迷期間的貸方需求轉化為發起股東額外流動性，而非新增生產能力。

印度銀行則利用政策支持窗口，以較低避險成本在海外籌資。ICICI Bank先與美國銀行簽訂約$10億貸款後，進一步啟動規模約$14.5億的聯貸案。這筆4年期融資的利率為SOFR加碼110個基點，並可能隨更多貸款機構加入而擴大。

印度央行向符合資格的銀行及國營企業提供固定年利率1.5%的外匯交換，平均期限至少3年，低於當前市場避險成本。窗口將於12月31日關閉，促使借款人提前籌措美元資金。自6月8日開放至7月底，印度銀行已透過國際債券及貸款籌得$25.8億。

資產負債表受損的借款人可用選項則少得多。Bally’s週五在監管申報文件中表示，公司能否繼續經營存在重大疑慮，因為現行預測顯示其流動性與槓桿將不符合貸款人要求。這家賭場營運商正商討出售資產、發行股票及債務融資，但目前均未解除違反契約條款的風險。

7月的一份條款清單可協助Bally’s為布朗克斯賭場開發案及其他需求籌資，但不具約束力。公司已投入逾$8億，並預計再為該專案籌措超過$5億。第2季營收成長21%至$7.92億，符合分析師平均預期，然而單憑營收增加，仍不足以提供解除警示所需的流動性或契約緩衝空間。

Raizen的債務重整進度較快，但營運表現仍不均衡。債權人已批准規模650億雷亞爾、約合$125億的重整案，法院也在7月確認該計畫。這家巴西集團正拆分為燃料配送及糖與乙醇兩項業務，管理層承諾簡化業務組合並提高資本結構效率。

燃料配送部門的季度調整後息稅折舊攤銷前盈餘為35.4億雷亞爾，超過一年前的3倍。糖業務仍然疲弱，銷量下降11%、價格不如預期，異常降雨也影響糖廠；乙醇銷量雖增加24%，但低價限制了效益。這項分歧說明，重整在法律程序上完成，並不會消除支撐重整後債務所需的營運工作。

## AI擔保將信用風險移出資產負債表

AI融資快速成長，為信用投資人帶來另一項挑戰：在科技週期反轉前，或許不會以傳統債務形式呈現的或有義務。與大型AI公司相關的剩餘價值擔保約有$700億已置於其申報資產負債表之外，而Nvidia擬議的融資合作可能再將這類架構擴大數百億美元。

典型交易由特殊目的公司舉債購買晶片或建置運算容量，再以使用者的合約付款償還債務。若客戶停止付款，債權人會先嘗試出租或出售設備，剩餘價值擔保則彌補其後仍存在的缺口。這類擔保可提高評級並降低客戶融資成本，科技供應商也不必在交易初期將其認列為一般融資債務。

問題在於，這項安排會在技術及轉售風險最昂貴時將其移轉給擔保人。AI景氣繁榮時，需求強勁且債務迅速攤還，擔保看似不太可能被動用；一旦景氣反轉，客戶可能違約，晶片價格與次級市場需求也可能同步下跌，迫使供應商在本身獲利承壓時履行付款義務。

Nvidia表示，將視個別案件情況，為單一投資機會提供最高25%的剩餘價值支持。這項上限意味公司提出的$5,000億融資計畫，不能被解讀為承諾替整體金額的四分之一提供資金。然而，債權人仍須評估Nvidia能同時支持多少專案，以及在壓力情境下將如何評價快速折舊的設備。

Meta較早透過路易斯安那州Hyperion資料中心約$270億債務，以及德州Sopaipilla專案約$130億債務，建立了先例。如果Meta選擇提前退出長期租約，相關擔保就會發揮作用，因此風險主要取決於Meta本身的決策與信用能力。

Broadcom則將這套架構延伸至客戶融資。在一筆$350億交易中，包括Apollo與Blackstone在內的投資人為客製化晶片提供融資，再將晶片租給Anthropic，Broadcom為其中大部分提供擔保。擔保協助優先順位券別取得投資級評級，但也使Broadcom的或有曝險與客戶的行為及償債能力相連。

美國銀行策略師估計，包含該交易在內的較大型平台，到2029年年中可能累積$3,700億優先債務。單筆擔保對資本實力雄厚的晶片製造商或許易於承擔，但一系列相互重疊的融資，即使尚未有任何擔保遭到求償，也可能限制公司的財務彈性。

評級機構已將這些累積承諾視為具有實質經濟意義的債務。標普認為Broadcom的剩餘價值支持屬於類債務的或有義務，因此納入調整後債務。穆迪則警告，即使申報的融資債務槓桿偏低，若此類承諾大幅增加，仍可能削弱Broadcom的財務彈性並拖累其信用狀況。

晶片融資一般約在5年內攤還，符合設備使用年限短、折舊快速的特性。隨本金償還，受擔保金額會逐步下降，使貸方的風險期間短於大型資料中心動輒數十年的租約。但承銷判斷也因而更加集中：現金流必須在新世代硬體大幅侵蝕擔保品價值前清償債務。

並非所有信用投資人都預期擔保會被動用。若運算token需求持續成長、產能仍然短缺，即使個別客戶無法履約，晶片也可重新配置。這些架構還會在法律文件中明列潛在義務，而不是隱藏其存在。尚未解決的問題是風險的相關性：若數名客戶因AI投資效益不如預期而同時陷入壓力，需求下降、客戶違約及設備價值下跌可能一併發生。

初級市場已在測試投資人願意為多少此類複雜性提供資金。Zenith Arc擁有Jane Street的長期租約支持，仍須為債務支付接近9%的殖利率；投資級發行人試圖壓縮利差後，則遭遇創紀錄的訂單流失。市場區分的不再只是發行人強弱，買方正依據現金流或擔保品價值不足時損失最終落在何處，分別評估直接企業債務、專案融資、租賃義務與或有擔保。

## 中國公共部門資產負債表填補民間信用真空

中國7月信用數據顯示，家庭與企業償還銀行債務之際，政府借款支撐了社會融資增量。實體經濟借款人的人民幣貸款淨償還5,900億元，創2002年有資料以來最大萎縮。若計入金融機構間貸款，整體貸款減少3,400億元，降幅超過經濟學家預測的3倍。

社會融資規模仍增加1.4兆元，高於預期，其中政府債券發行貢獻1.3兆元，民間部門對增量的貢獻所剩無幾。家庭與企業的長期貸款均告萎縮，與房地產需求疲弱及投資意願有限相符。

銀行通常在第2季末加速放款，因此7月貸款往往回落，但本次降幅已超過正常季節性。中國貸款萎縮過去相當罕見，隨家庭設法減債、薪資停滯，以及房地產與傳統基礎建設的預期報酬下降，如今發生頻率已提高。科技及新興產業比舊有的貸款密集型成長模式更依賴債券與股票融資，但這項轉變仍不足以完全解釋廣泛民間需求的疲弱。

這種融資結構使財政政策必須扮演更大角色。當信心及預期報酬偏低時，降低貸款利率無法迫使家庭購屋或企業投資。即使央行維持充裕流動性，若公共支出未進一步增強，銀行貸款成長仍可能持續放緩。政府債券已開始取代貸款，成為新增信用的主要來源。

中國人民銀行透過一次罕見的月中隔夜操作提供流動性。人行進行3,490億元隔夜逆回購；扣除10億元7天期合約到期後，銀行體系淨獲得3,480億元，為當月首次淨投放。此舉旨在平滑繳稅期間的資金狀況，而非預示全面寬鬆週期。

中國10年期公債殖利率下降1個基點至1.68%，創2025年7月以來最低；強勁需求也使10年期公債標售殖利率降至一年多來最低。人行另計畫進行1兆元、6個月期買斷式逆回購，完全抵銷等額到期合約。

這套操作有利於債券持有收益，卻不是不分對象的流動性注入。先前曾在6月底及7月底使用的隔夜工具，使央行能更精準地調節短期市場狀況。政策制定者因銀行利潤率承壓，仍不願調降政策利率，自2025年5月以來一直維持不變。

因此，中國債市上漲源於兩項相互關聯但不同的發展：人行降低短期資金緊縮風險，信用數據則顯示民間借款意願的疲弱程度更深。前者鼓勵投資人持有債券；後者進一步強化市場預期，即政府發債與支出將不得不扮演更多原本由家庭與企業信貸承擔的融資角色。

## 財政承諾與政策分歧重塑全球債市

印尼將市場密切關注的財政承諾轉化為正式預算目標。總統Prabowo Subianto提議，明年財政赤字占國內生產毛額比率由2026年預估的2.85%降至2.4%，同時追求6%的經濟成長。政府支出僅相對溫和地增加4%至4,097兆印尼盾，收入則預計成長7%。

印尼債券、印尼盾及股票週五走強，顯示這場演說並未加劇市場對財政失控的疑慮。印尼債市今年曾成為亞洲表現最差的市場，匯率也徘徊在歷史低點附近，因此財政審慎格外重要。Prabowo亦引用標普確認印尼評級，作為債務可持續性的證據，但惠譽與穆迪仍維持負向展望。

實際執行比表面目標更困難。預算假設美元兌印尼盾平均匯率為17,500，油價為每桶$75。上半年中央政府支出較一年前增加近30%，燃料與電力補貼、交通折扣及食品援助協助維持5.45%的經濟成長。免費供餐計畫在現行預算中的成本為$130億，村落合作社預計在6年內還需$130億。

Prabowo承諾改革採購制度、加強管控國營企業，並削減包括旗艦計畫在內的浪費。他還表示，國營企業今年應繳交200兆印尼盾股利，比2025年高40%。這些措施可能創造財政空間，但政府先前已將赤字預測上修至接近3%的法定上限，因此投資人仍有理由以實際執行結果檢驗收入與節支假設。

面對成長轉弱，菲律賓釋出不同的政策訊號。菲律賓中央銀行總裁Eli Remolona表示，經濟已經放緩，央行抗通膨的手段將不再那麼激進，但在放鬆政策立場前，仍需要看到物價呈現更有說服力的下降趨勢。貨幣當局今年已升息50個基點，下次會議定於8月27日。

官方第2季經濟成長率為2.3%，是2009年底以來除疫情期間外最疲弱的表現。Remolona認為，前一年防洪支出扭曲了比較基準，估計基礎成長率較接近3.2%；但相較經濟5.5%的成長潛力，他仍形容這一速度偏弱。由於截至第2季支出比一年前低約7%，總統Ferdinand Marcos Jr.承諾加快基礎建設招標，並在第4季追趕公共支出進度。

澳洲市場的政策方向相反。交換市場反映澳洲央行截至11月升息25個基點的機率約為45%，高於最近一次會議前的38%。澳洲央行一致決議將現金利率維持在4.35%，但總裁Michele Bullock表示，由於通膨仍高於2%至3%的目標，再度升息很有可能。

投資人將部位由短天期債券轉向10年期債券，以區分近期再度升息的風險，與現行限制性政策最終造成的效果。部分經理人認為，隨失業率上升、房市信心轉弱，今年3次升息已經足夠；包括BlackRock在內的其他投資人則預期，若通膨比預測更具持續性，11月仍會再升息一次。

日本同樣存在近期緊縮預期，但匯率干預增添了市場波動。日圓週五一度升值0.2%至159.15兌1美元，仍接近市場關注官方是否採取行動的160關卡。隔夜交換反映日本央行9月升息機率約80%，並完全反映10月前升息一次。

這些預期仍未消除以日圓融資的利差交易。日圓已回吐7月底美日聯合干預帶來的大部分升幅，投資人並利用匯率反彈至157附近重新建立美元兌日圓部位。日本1%的政策利率仍遠低於其他已開發市場可取得的報酬，財政疑慮也增添壓力；日本央行即使升息一次，也只能小幅縮小利差。

全球轉變的範圍遠超過聯準會政策辯論。在32個交換市場中，約三分之二已反映升息，交易員預計未來一年7個主要市場合計將緊縮約400個基點。能源成本上升、財政擴張及AI相關投資需求對各國的影響不同，但整體結果是貨幣政策分歧程度下降，減少了債券投資人過去可用於分散風險的空間。

新興市場融資環境仍讓部分政府得以減少高成本債務。肯亞計畫在12月底前發行$8.15億歐洲債券，作為截至2027年6月、總額$54億的外部融資計畫之一。整套方案另包括$3億熊貓債、$5億伊斯蘭債券，以及與世界糧食計畫署進行、由美國國際開發金融公司支持的$10億債務換糧食交易。

肯亞打算透過負債管理操作償還至少$5億高成本外債。非洲主權債利差平均約比美債高300個基點，低於3月底的405個基點，使發行人得以對市場融資成本顯著較高時舉借的債務進行再融資。國際貨幣基金仍將肯亞列為債務困境高風險國家，因此新借款的成本與期限，比重新取得市場融資本身更為重要。

隨主權債殖利率下降，哥倫比亞本地公司債市場也重新開放。2026年前7個月，企業發債約4兆披索，約合$12.7億，超過2025年全年。發行仍集中於辦理再融資的銀行，但Metro de Medellin已透過10年、14年及30年期通膨連結債券籌得約$1億，殖利率介於7.19%至7.29%。

市場友善的政府上台後，哥倫比亞2028年到期主權債殖利率維持在12.2%附近，低於5月的14.7%。然而，6%的通膨率及接近12%的短期殖利率仍限制非金融業借款人，地震重建也可能使政府財政計畫更加複雜。市場確已重啟，卻仍是建立在主權債殖利率下降之上的選擇性市場，並不代表企業融資成本普遍低廉。

## 前瞻市場意義

新一週的首要問題，是中東局勢最新升級會否延續週五油價與美債行情的逆轉。美國預計公布更多對伊朗經濟措施的細節，停火協議則將於週一到期，目前看來各方尚未就荷莫茲海峽達成協議。與其將措施形容為前所未有，投資人更應關注限制內容、對出口及航運的影響，以及德黑蘭的回應。

週五美股收盤後的發展提高了事件風險，但不能用來解釋已完成的當日行情。以色列空襲黎巴嫩南部造成11人死亡，其中包括一名真主黨高階指揮官，使原已停滯的美伊談判更加複雜。布蘭特原油在週一亞洲早盤一度升至接近$89，其後回吐部分漲幅。若荷莫茲海峽持續暢通、保險及運費下降，油價也回吐全週漲幅，將有助維持近期通膨改善趨勢；若軍事干擾進一步擴大，或供給遭到有效限制，損益兩平通膨率與央行政策預期均將承壓。

美國財政部週三將標售$160億、20年期公債，對市場承接長天期利率風險的意願構成另一項直接考驗。20年期殖利率週五在5.25%附近交易，新券發行前市場指示水準約為5.27%；若標售結果落在該水準，將是2020年恢復此期限債券以來最高得標殖利率。結果必須與標售前自身水準比較：若出現尾差，表示繼成本高昂的10年及30年期標售後，投資人仍要求更大讓利；若結果穩健，則代表5.25%以上的殖利率正吸引買盤。

同樣於週三公布的聯準會7月底會議紀錄，將說明以9票對3票維持利率不變背後的分歧。週五零售及信心數據加強了等待的理由，但Goolsbee要求再看到數次有利通膨數據，也顯示一週的溫和數字仍然不足。會議紀錄可釐清，在最新數據公布前，官員對通膨持續性的疑慮有多普遍，以及3張反對票是否代表一個持久的政策陣營。

週二公布的新屋開工及工業生產，將協助判斷經濟是由消費帶動放緩，還是已出現更廣泛的疲弱。本週稍晚公布的8月製造業採購經理人初值，則將檢驗工廠活動是否仍處於擴張。8月26日的核心個人消費支出通膨仍是更具決定性的物價數據，因為其中服務業組成可顯示近期通膨降溫是否已超越能源敏感型類別。

中國週一的經濟活動數據將檢驗政府融資是否正轉化為需求。零售銷售年增率預計加快至1.5%，工業生產年增率則預測放緩至4.9%，房地產及固定資產投資的跌幅可能進一步擴大。在民間貸款出現創紀錄萎縮後，即使人行繼續偏好流動性管理而非調降政策利率，疲弱的經濟活動仍會加大財政支持壓力。

日本週一公布的第2季經濟成長率，預計在內需帶動下達到年化2%。若數據更強，將鞏固市場反映約80%的9月升息機率，並檢驗緊縮政策能否比匯率干預更持久地支撐日圓。若消費疲弱，日本央行則須在匯率與進口物價壓力，以及對脆弱家庭需求升息的風險之間取得平衡。

英國週三公布的通膨率預計年增2.9%，將是4個月來首次加速，原因包括家庭能源帳單及AI相關記憶體晶片短缺推升價格。截至6月的3個月，不含獎金的薪資成長率預計維持3.4%，失業率則小幅降至4.8%。這組數據將決定英格蘭銀行能否忽略外部能源及電子產品成本，或必須更重視這些成本向國內通膨擴散的風險。

在代理總裁Destry Damayanti領導下，市場預期印尼央行週三將政策利率維持在5.75%。投資人將比較新領導層的政策指引，與Prabowo提出的2.4%赤字目標，以及收入、油價和印尼盾匯率假設。若央行維持利率並強調獨立性，可望延續市場對預算案的正面初步反應；若在財政節支尚未獲得證明前便面臨寬鬆壓力，則會再度引發市場對印尼財政與貨幣政策組合的疑慮。

信用市場方面，預估投資級債發行量減少，將檢驗創紀錄的訂單流失只是發行日程擁擠下的短期反應，還是更持久重新定價的開端。投資人在兩週內吸收了$1,360億供給，但發行人過度壓低定價時便撤回訂單。下一批交易將顯示，發行步調放緩能否讓借款人重拾定價能力，或美債殖利率、AI資本需求及或有負債已提高全市場要求的最低補償。

overall_summary.headline: 消費轉弱降低近期聯準會升息風險，油價卻逆轉美債漲勢
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美債早盤漲勢逆轉，各期限殖利率收盤全面走高。2年期殖利率上升2.8個基點至4.171%，10年期上升4.9個基點至4.693%，30年期上升4.6個基點至5.261%；2年與10年期利差擴大2.1個基點至52.2個基點。10年期殖利率的漲幅幾乎由實質利率與預期通膨各占一半：實質殖利率上升2.5個基點，損益兩平通膨率增加2.4個基點。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries reversed an early, data-driven rally on Aug. 14 as a renewed oil advance and the prospect of harsher US pressure on Iran restored inflation compensation and left the long end carrying the burden of fiscal supply. July retail sales fell 0.6%, the largest decline in more than a year, and preliminary August consumer sentiment dropped to 51 against a consensus of 55. Those reports briefly pushed the 2-year yield below 4.10% and encouraged traders to reduce expectations for a Federal Reserve increase in September. By the completed close, however, yields were higher across the curve.

The 2-year yield rose 2.8 basis points to 4.171%, while the 5-year increased 4.8 basis points to 4.365%, the 10-year climbed 4.9 basis points to 4.693% and the 30-year added 4.6 basis points to 5.261%. The 2s10s curve steepened 2.1 basis points to 52.2 basis points, and 2s30s widened 1.8 basis points to 109 basis points. The session preserved some distinction between reduced near-term tightening risk and the compensation required farther out, but it was not a simple front-end rally: the reversal in energy and inflation pricing was large enough to lift even policy-sensitive yields by the close.

The 10-year nominal move was almost evenly divided between real rates and expected inflation. The 10-year real yield rose 2.5 basis points to 2.41%, while the 10-year breakeven increased 2.4 basis points to 2.283%. That composition captured the day’s competing evidence. Weaker spending lowered the probability that domestic demand alone would force an immediate Fed response, but it did not remove the real financing pressure associated with deficits, heavy public and corporate borrowing, or the possibility that a renewed energy shock would interrupt the recent improvement in inflation.

Oil supplied the reversal. WTI rose 1.42% to $82.40 and Brent gained 1.67% to $88.52 after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent promised additional economic measures against Iran in the coming week while the US maintained its blockade of Iranian ports. Brent finished almost 6% higher over the week. The escalation took on greater significance because July consumer and producer inflation had benefited from retreating energy costs. Friday’s crude advance did not rewrite those released data, but it raised the risk that their favorable energy contribution will prove temporary.

The broader market registered caution rather than a disorderly flight from risk. The S&P 500 fell 0.17%, the Nasdaq 100 declined 0.13% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 0.31%. The dollar index weakened 0.29%, while gold futures rose 0.39% to $4,380.40. Long-duration assets absorbed the clearest damage: an index of Treasuries with maturities of 20 years or more fell 0.71%, and long-dated investment-grade corporate-bond indexes lost roughly three-quarters of a percent. Those moves reflected their benchmark-duration exposure as well as a more demanding primary-market environment.

The session’s character was therefore a reversal of relief, not a repudiation of the softer data. Traders continued to remove September tightening wagers after a week of weaker employment, benign consumer and producer inflation, and Friday’s decline in spending. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee also acknowledged that the last three months of inflation had become more encouraging. Yet he wanted another three or four months resembling June before becoming confident that inflation was returning to 2%, while oil, Treasury supply and a widening range of AI-related financing demands kept longer-term borrowing costs elevated.

## Consumers Weaken, but Oil Reclaims the Rates Narrative

The July retail report showed a meaningful loss of momentum after a stronger first half. The value of purchases fell 0.6%, led by a 2.2% decline at non-store retailers and a 1.8% drop at motor-vehicle and parts dealers. Five of the 13 categories declined. Restaurants and bars, the report’s only service category, increased 0.5%, preventing the release from becoming evidence of a uniformly weak consumer, but the breadth and concentration of the declines were sufficient to raise concern about discretionary demand.

Some of the reversal may have reflected calendar distortion. Amazon moved its Prime Day event to June from July a year earlier, pulling some online purchases into the preceding month. That qualification matters for interpreting the 2.2% fall in non-store sales, but it does not erase the simultaneous decline in autos or the deterioration in sentiment. The University of Michigan’s preliminary index fell to 51 in August, 4 points below the median forecast, leaving households markedly less confident even as the latest inflation readings improved.

The consumer’s financial cushion has also become thinner. The personal saving rate was 2.7% in June, less than half its level two years earlier and close to the low end of a series extending to 1947. Inflation had recently outpaced average hourly earnings on a year-over-year basis, reducing the amount some households could set aside. Rising stock-market wealth has supported spending among asset owners, but continued consumption growth cannot indefinitely depend on a falling saving rate without households borrowing or selling assets.

That background makes the July sales decline more consequential than an isolated weak monthly print. It does not establish a recession or a sustained contraction in consumption, especially when one major promotional event shifted into June. It does show that households have less room to absorb another round of energy or goods-price pressure without reducing other purchases. The immediate bond response reflected that risk: short Treasuries rallied and the 2-year yield briefly traded at its lowest since June 30.

Interest-rate contracts showed investors exiting both September hike wagers and expectations for more than one increase by the middle of 2027. At one point, only about 8 basis points of tightening remained priced for September, down from nearly 19 basis points on July 31. The repricing extended a sequence that began with weak July employment data on Aug. 7 and accelerated after benign consumer and producer inflation.

Goolsbee’s comments reinforced the case for patience while resisting the conclusion that the inflation problem had been solved. He supported holding rates steady at the July meeting and described growth and the labor market as broadly stable. Inflation remained his primary concern after five or six months of unfavorable readings, but the Chicago Fed president regarded the past three months as encouraging evidence that tariff and oil shocks may be passing through.

His condition for greater confidence was demanding: three or four more months resembling June. Goolsbee emphasized that inflation has remained above target for more than five years and that previous high-inflation episodes became difficult and costly to reverse. He also said a multi-month fall in retail sales would make him nervous, preserving a separate growth threshold rather than treating one weak report as decisive.

The July meeting had already exposed a more hawkish coalition, with three policymakers dissenting in favor of a 25-basis-point increase. Friday’s evidence weakened the immediate case for joining them, but Goolsbee’s position was not an argument for easing. It was a case for waiting long enough to determine whether recent inflation relief has breadth and persistence while monitoring whether softer hiring and spending develop into a more serious demand slowdown.

Oil prevented that waiting argument from producing a durable Treasury rally. Bessent said the US would announce measures in the coming week intended to intensify Iran’s economic isolation, alongside the continued blockade of Iranian ports. Brent traded near $87 during part of Friday before finishing at $88.52. The prospect of tighter constraints on Iranian trade shifted attention back from released July inflation to the cost of energy entering future data.

The resulting selloff was not confined to breakevens. Higher real yields indicated that investors also demanded more compensation for owning duration amid heavy financing needs. The recently completed $25 billion 30-year auction had cleared at 5.216%, the highest borrowing rate for such a sale since 2001, and Friday’s market close put the long-bond yield another 4.5 basis points above that level. The auction had been adequately covered, with a 2.39 bid-to-cover ratio close to the recent average, but it established demand at a high price rather than a willingness to absorb long duration at substantially lower yields.

That distinction remained visible across horizons. The 2-year yield was 2.5 basis points lower over the week, while the 10-year was 4.7 basis points higher and the 30-year had risen 5.9 basis points. Over one month, the 30-year yield was up 15.5 basis points, compared with a 2.4-basis-point decline in the 2-year. Near-term Fed expectations softened, but fiscal supply, energy uncertainty and competition for capital continued to steepen the curve.

## Credit Buyers Push Back After the Issuance Wave

The same demand for compensation became more explicit in the US investment-grade market. Investors withdrew about 36% of their initial orders for high-grade bond sales during the week after issuers tightened final pricing, twice the previous week’s attrition rate and well above the 22% average for the year. Attrition reached 45% on Thursday, the highest recorded in 2026.

Advanced Micro Devices provided the clearest example. Orders for the longest tranche of its $4.75 billion offering fell by more than half after the company reduced its borrowing spread. The bonds were still placed, and overall demand for investment-grade credit remained healthy, but investors demonstrated that large headline orderbooks were not firm commitments at every price.

The pushback followed $136 billion of issuance in two weeks, putting August on course to become the busiest on record for the month. Companies have been borrowing for acquisitions, refinancing and the AI infrastructure buildout, adding corporate duration just as Treasury yields remain near multiyear highs. Underwriters expected supply to slow to about $20 billion in the following week, giving investors a pause after the concentrated calendar.

Corporate funding conditions were still favorable by longer historical standards. Average investment-grade spreads were roughly 0.78 percentage point over Treasuries, and funds buying the debt attracted almost $3 billion in the week through Wednesday. The change was in bargaining power at the margin: investors continued to provide capital, but they were less willing to preserve oversized orders when borrowers attempted to extract the final few basis points of pricing.

Zenith Arc’s $2.25 billion green-bond sale illustrated both the availability and the cost of financing outside the investment-grade market. The joint venture between Fluidstack and Next Frontier priced 5-year notes at 99.5 cents on the dollar to yield almost 9%, at the wide end of earlier discussions. Moody’s rated the debt Ba2, two levels below investment grade.

The proceeds will fund construction of a data center and substation in central Oklahoma leased to a Jane Street subsidiary. The 15-year triple-net lease makes the tenant responsible for operating costs, taxes, utilities, insurance and power charges in addition to base rent, with a customary guaranty from Jane Street Group. Those contractual payments gave creditors a defined source of cash flow, but the wide-end pricing showed that investors still required substantial compensation for construction, technology and single-project exposure.

The deal also extended the use of green finance for data-center construction. Sustainable bond sales for such projects reached $11.2 billion in 2025, up from $7.6 billion in 2024, while Edged Compute and TeraWulf had already raised $1.3 billion and $3.2 billion, respectively. Environmental designation widened the potential investor base, but it did not make buyers indifferent to leverage or project risk.

A prospective €2 billion financing for Kedrion Biopharma showed cash-rich lenders considering a different use of leverage. The blood-plasma company was discussing debt with private-credit providers, with part of the proceeds potentially funding a dividend to owners including Permira and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority. The transaction remained under consideration rather than agreed. If completed, it would convert lender demand during a slow merger market into additional sponsor liquidity rather than new productive capacity.

Indian banks were using a policy-supported window to raise offshore money on cheaper hedging terms. ICICI Bank launched a syndicated loan of about $1.45 billion after initially signing roughly $1 billion with Bank of America. The 4-year facility carried a margin of 110 basis points over the Secured Overnight Financing Rate and could increase as more lenders joined.

The Reserve Bank of India is offering eligible banks and state enterprises a foreign-exchange swap at a fixed annual rate of 1.5% for average maturities of at least 3 years, below prevailing market hedging costs. The window closes on Dec. 31, encouraging borrowers to accelerate dollar funding. Indian banks had raised $2.58 billion in international bonds and loans between the facility’s June 8 opening and the end of July.

Borrowers with damaged balance sheets faced a much narrower set of options. Bally’s said in a Friday regulatory filing that there was substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern because current forecasts indicated it would fail lender requirements for liquidity and leverage. The casino operator was discussing asset sales, equity issuance and debt financing, but none had yet resolved the covenant risk.

A July term sheet could help fund Bally’s Bronx casino development and other needs, but it was non-binding. The company expects to raise more than $500 million for the project after already investing more than $800 million. Second-quarter revenue rose 21% to $792 million, meeting analysts’ average estimate, yet the increase did not by itself provide the liquidity or covenant headroom required to remove the warning.

Raizen was further along in a debt overhaul but still exposed to uneven operations. Creditors had approved a restructuring of 65 billion reais, or $12.5 billion, and a court confirmed the plan in July. The Brazilian group is being separated into fuel distribution and sugar-and-ethanol businesses, with management promising simpler portfolios and more efficient capital structures.

Its fuel-distribution unit produced adjusted quarterly earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization of 3.54 billion reais, more than triple the year-earlier result. The sugar business remained weak as volumes fell 11%, prices disappointed and unusual rain affected mills. Ethanol volumes rose 24%, but low prices limited the benefit. The divergence showed why legal completion of a restructuring does not eliminate the operating work needed to support the resulting debt.

## AI Backstops Move Credit Risk Beyond the Balance Sheet

The rapid growth of AI financing is creating a separate challenge for credit investors: contingent obligations that may not appear as conventional debt until the technology cycle turns. Roughly $70 billion of residual-value guarantees associated with major AI companies already sit outside their reported balance sheets, and Nvidia’s proposed financing partnerships could expand the structure by tens of billions of dollars.

A typical transaction uses a special-purpose vehicle to borrow for the purchase of chips or construction of computing capacity. Contractual payments from the user service the debt. If the customer stops paying, creditors first attempt to lease or sell the equipment; a residual-value backstop covers any remaining shortfall. The guarantee can improve ratings and reduce the customer’s financing cost without requiring the technology supplier to record ordinary funded debt at inception.

The arrangement transfers technology and resale risk to the guarantor precisely when that risk could become most expensive. During an AI boom, strong demand and rapid amortization make the guarantee appear remote. In a downturn, customers could default while chip prices and secondary demand fall together, forcing suppliers to make payments when their own earnings are under pressure.

Nvidia said it may provide residual-value support for as much as 25% of an individual opportunity on a case-by-case basis. The limitation prevents the company’s headline $500 billion financing initiative from being read as a promise to fund one-quarter of the entire amount. It still leaves creditors assessing how many projects could be supported simultaneously and how Nvidia would value rapidly depreciating equipment under stressed conditions.

Meta established an earlier template through roughly $27 billion of debt for its Hyperion data center in Louisiana and about $13 billion for its Sopaipilla project in Texas. Its guarantees become relevant if the company elects to leave long leases early. That condition ties the risk primarily to Meta’s own decision and credit capacity.

Broadcom extended the structure to customer financing. It backstopped most of a $35 billion transaction in which investors including Apollo and Blackstone financed custom chips to be leased to Anthropic. The guarantee helped senior tranches obtain investment-grade ratings, but it also linked Broadcom’s contingent exposure to the actions and solvency of a customer.

Bank of America strategists estimated that the broader platform containing that transaction could accumulate $370 billion of senior debt by the middle of 2029. A single guarantee may be manageable for a strongly capitalized chipmaker; a series of overlapping financings could constrain flexibility even before any one backstop is called.

Ratings agencies are treating that accumulation as economically relevant debt. S&P considers Broadcom’s residual-value support a contingent debt-like obligation and includes it in adjusted debt. Moody’s warned that a substantial increase in such commitments could reduce Broadcom’s financial flexibility and weigh on its credit profile despite low leverage on reported funded obligations.

Chip financings generally amortize over about 5 years, matching the short useful life and rapid depreciation of the equipment. That schedule reduces the guaranteed amount as principal is repaid, giving lenders a shorter risk horizon than the multi-decade leases used for major data centers. It also concentrates the underwriting question: cash flow must retire the obligation before newer generations of hardware significantly erode the collateral value.

Not every credit investor expects the guarantees to be used. Continued growth in demand for computing tokens and a shortage of capacity would allow chips to be redeployed even if an individual customer failed. The structures also make potential obligations visible in legal documents rather than hiding their existence. The unresolved issue is correlation. If several customers encounter stress because the economics of AI investment disappoint, declining demand, customer defaults and falling equipment values would arrive together.

The primary market is already testing how much of that complexity investors will finance. Zenith Arc paid almost 9% for debt backed by a long Jane Street lease, while investment-grade borrowers faced record order attrition after attempting to compress spreads. The distinction is no longer simply between strong and weak issuers. Buyers are separating direct corporate debt, project finance, lease obligations and contingent guarantees according to where losses return when cash flow or collateral values fall short.

## China’s Public Balance Sheet Fills a Private Credit Vacuum

China’s July credit data showed government borrowing sustaining aggregate finance while households and businesses repaid bank debt. Borrowers in the real economy made net repayments of 590 billion yuan in local-currency loans, the largest contraction in data extending to 2002. Including lending between financial institutions, overall loans declined by 340 billion yuan, more than three times the decrease economists had forecast.

Aggregate financing nevertheless increased by 1.4 trillion yuan, exceeding expectations. Government-bond issuance accounted for 1.3 trillion yuan of that amount, leaving little private contribution to the expansion. Both household and corporate long-term loans contracted, consistent with weak property demand and limited appetite for investment.

July lending normally falls after banks accelerate credit at the end of the second quarter, but the scale of the decline went beyond ordinary seasonality. Loan contractions were once rare in China and have become more frequent as households seek to reduce debt, wages stagnate and expected returns on property and conventional infrastructure fall. Technology and newer industries rely more on bonds and equity than the older loan-intensive growth model, but that shift does not fully explain the weakness in broad private demand.

The composition creates a larger role for fiscal policy. Lower lending rates cannot compel households to buy homes or companies to invest when confidence and expected returns remain poor. Without stronger public spending, bank-loan growth can continue to slow even if the central bank maintains ample liquidity. Government bonds are already replacing loans as the dominant source of new credit.

The People’s Bank of China supplied that liquidity with an unusual mid-month overnight operation. It conducted 349 billion yuan of overnight reverse repos; after a 1 billion yuan maturity in 7-day contracts, the banking system received a net 348 billion yuan, its first net addition of the month. The operation was designed to smooth funding around tax payments rather than signal a broad easing cycle.

China’s 10-year government-bond yield fell 1 basis point to 1.68%, its lowest since July 2025, and strong demand pushed the yield at a 10-year sovereign auction to the lowest in more than a year. The PBOC also planned 1 trillion yuan of 6-month outright reverse repos, fully offsetting an equal amount of maturing contracts.

The combination was supportive for carry without constituting an indiscriminate liquidity injection. The overnight tool, previously used near the end of June and July, gave the central bank greater precision over short-term conditions. Policymakers remain reluctant to cut the policy rate because of pressure on bank profit margins and have kept it unchanged since May 2025.

China’s bond rally therefore rested on two related but distinct developments: the PBOC reduced the risk of a temporary funding squeeze, while the credit data revealed a deeper shortage of willing private borrowers. The first encouraged investors to hold bonds; the second reinforced expectations that government issuance and spending will have to do more of the work normally performed by household and corporate credit.

## Fiscal Promises and Policy Divergence Reshape Global Debt

Indonesia converted a closely watched fiscal promise into a formal budget target. President Prabowo Subianto proposed narrowing the deficit to 2.4% of gross domestic product next year from an expected 2.85% in 2026, while seeking 6% economic growth. State expenditure would rise a relatively modest 4% to 4,097 trillion rupiah, and revenue was projected to increase 7%.

Indonesian bonds, the rupiah and equities strengthened on Friday, indicating that the speech did not intensify concerns about fiscal slippage. The caution mattered after the bond market had become Asia’s worst performer during the year and the currency had hovered near a record low. Prabowo also cited S&P’s affirmation of Indonesia’s rating as evidence of debt sustainability, though Fitch and Moody’s retained negative outlooks.

Execution remains more difficult than the headline target. The budget assumes an average exchange rate of 17,500 rupiah per dollar and oil at $75 a barrel. Central-government spending rose almost 30% from a year earlier in the first half as fuel and electricity subsidies, transport discounts and food support helped sustain 5.45% growth. The free-meal program costs $13 billion in the current budget, while village cooperatives are expected to require another $13 billion over 6 years.

Prabowo promised procurement reform, tighter control of state enterprises and the elimination of waste even in flagship programs. He also said state companies should remit 200 trillion rupiah in dividends this year, 40% more than in 2025. Those measures could create fiscal space, but the administration’s previous deficit estimate had already been revised toward the legal ceiling of 3%, giving investors reason to test revenue and savings assumptions against actual execution.

The Philippines signaled a different response to weaker growth. Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Governor Eli Remolona said the central bank would be less aggressive in fighting inflation because the economy had slowed, while still requiring a more convincing downward trend in prices before relaxing its stance. Monetary authorities have raised rates by 50 basis points this year and meet next on Aug. 27.

Official Q2 growth was 2.3%, the weakest outside the pandemic since late 2009. Remolona argued that the comparison was distorted by flood-control spending in the prior year and estimated underlying growth closer to 3.2%, but he still described that pace as weak relative to the economy’s 5.5% capacity. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. promised faster infrastructure bidding and a catch-up in public spending by Q4 after expenditure ran about 7% below the year-earlier pace through Q2.

Australia’s market moved in the opposite policy direction. Swaps priced about a 45% probability of a 25-basis-point Reserve Bank increase by November, up from 38% before the latest meeting. The RBA unanimously kept its cash rate at 4.35%, but Governor Michele Bullock said another increase was quite possible because inflation remained above the 2%-to-3% target.

Positioning shifted away from short maturities and toward 10-year debt as investors distinguished the risk of another near-term increase from the eventual effect of already restrictive policy. Some managers judged that three increases this year were sufficient as unemployment rose and housing sentiment weakened. Others, including BlackRock, expected another move in November if inflation proved more persistent than forecast.

Japan presented a similar near-term tightening expectation but with currency intervention adding volatility. The yen strengthened as much as 0.2% to 159.15 per dollar on Friday, staying close to the 160 area watched for official action. Overnight swaps assigned about an 80% probability to a Bank of Japan increase in September and fully priced a move by October.

Those expectations had not eliminated the yen-funded carry trade. The currency had surrendered much of the gain produced by the late-July joint US-Japan intervention, and investors used the rebound toward 157 to rebuild dollar-yen positions. Japan’s 1% policy rate remained far below returns available in other developed markets, while fiscal concerns added pressure. A single BOJ increase would narrow the differential only modestly.

The global shift is broader than the Fed debate. Across 32 swap markets, about two-thirds were priced for rate increases, with traders expecting roughly 400 basis points of combined tightening across 7 major markets over the following year. Higher energy costs, fiscal expansion and AI-related investment demand are affecting countries differently, but the aggregate result is less monetary-policy divergence than bond investors once relied upon for diversification.

Emerging-market financing conditions still allowed some governments to reduce expensive debt. Kenya planned an $815 million Eurobond by the end of December as part of a $5.4 billion external-financing program through June 2027. The package also included a $300 million panda bond, a $500 million sukuk and a $1 billion debt-for-food swap with the World Food Programme backed by the US International Development Finance Corp.

Kenya intended to retire at least $500 million of high-cost external debt through liability-management operations. African sovereign spreads averaged about 300 basis points over Treasuries, down from 405 basis points at the end of March, enabling issuers to refinance debt raised when market access was substantially more expensive. Kenya remains classified by the International Monetary Fund as being at high risk of debt distress, making the cost and maturity of the new borrowing more important than the reopening of access alone.

Colombia’s local corporate market also reopened as sovereign yields fell. Companies sold about 4 trillion pesos, or $1.27 billion, during the first 7 months of 2026, more than in all of 2025. Issuance remained concentrated among banks refinancing debt, but Metro de Medellin raised about $100 million through 10-, 14- and 30-year inflation-linked bonds yielding between 7.19% and 7.29%.

The yield on Colombia’s sovereign bonds maturing in 2028 held near 12.2%, down from 14.7% in May, after a market-friendly government took office. Inflation of 6% and short-term yields near 12% continued to constrain non-financial borrowers, while earthquake reconstruction threatened to complicate the administration’s fiscal program. The reopening was real, but it remained a selective market built on lower sovereign yields rather than uniformly cheap corporate funding.

## Forward Market Significance

The first question for the new week is whether the latest Middle East escalation sustains Friday’s reversal in oil and Treasuries. The US is expected to provide details of its additional economic measures against Iran, while the ceasefire is due to expire Monday without an apparent agreement on the Strait of Hormuz. The content of the restrictions, their effect on exports and shipping, and the response from Tehran matter more than the description of the measures as unprecedented.

Developments after Friday’s US close increased the event risk without explaining that completed session. Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed 11 people, including a senior Hezbollah commander, and complicated already-stalled US-Iran negotiations. Brent rose as high as almost $89 in early Monday Asian trading before paring the move. Sustained passage through Hormuz, falling insurance and freight costs, and a reversal of the weekly crude gain would protect the recent improvement in inflation. Further military disruption or effective constraints on supply would leave both breakevens and central-bank expectations exposed.

Treasury faces another direct duration test on Wednesday with a scheduled $16 billion sale of 20-year bonds. The tenor traded near 5.25% on Friday, while the new security indicated around 5.27% in the when-issued market. If realized at auction, that would be the highest award since the maturity was reintroduced in 2020. The result must be judged against its own pre-sale level: a tail would indicate that investors still require a larger concession after the costly 10- and 30-year auctions, while a firm result would show that yields above 5.25% are attracting demand.

The Fed’s late-July meeting minutes, also due Wednesday, will clarify the divide behind the 9-3 vote to hold rates steady. Friday’s retail and sentiment data strengthened the case for waiting, but Goolsbee’s demand for several more favorable inflation readings showed why one week of benign releases is insufficient. The minutes can establish how widely officials shared concern about inflation persistence before the latest data and whether the three dissents reflected a durable coalition.

Housing starts and industrial production on Tuesday will help separate a consumer-led slowdown from broader weakness. Preliminary August manufacturing purchasing-manager data at the end of the week will test whether factory activity remains expansionary. Core personal-consumption-expenditures inflation on Aug. 26 remains the more decisive price release because its services composition will show whether the recent moderation extends beyond energy-sensitive categories.

China’s Monday activity data will test whether government finance is translating into demand. Retail-sales growth is expected to accelerate to 1.5% from a year earlier, while industrial-output growth is forecast to slow to 4.9% and declines in property and fixed-asset investment are expected to deepen. After private loans contracted by a record amount, weak activity would increase pressure for fiscal support even if the PBOC continues to favor liquidity management over policy-rate cuts.

Japan’s Q2 growth release on Monday is expected to show a 2% annualized expansion, led by domestic demand. A stronger result would reinforce the roughly 80% market probability of a September BOJ increase and test whether tighter policy can support the yen more durably than intervention. A weak consumption result would leave the central bank balancing currency and import-price pressure against the risk of tightening into fragile household demand.

UK inflation on Wednesday is forecast to rise 2.9% from a year earlier, the first acceleration in 4 months, as household energy bills and an AI-related memory-chip shortage lift prices. Wage growth excluding bonuses is expected to hold at 3.4% in the 3 months through June, with unemployment edging down to 4.8%. The combination will determine whether the Bank of England can look through external energy and electronics costs or must place greater weight on the risk that they spread into domestic inflation.

Bank Indonesia is expected to keep its policy rate at 5.75% on Wednesday under acting Governor Destry Damayanti. Investors will compare the new leadership’s guidance with Prabowo’s 2.4% deficit target and assumptions for revenue, oil and the rupiah. Holding the rate while maintaining an independence-focused message would support the favorable initial reaction to the budget; pressure for easier policy before the fiscal savings are demonstrated would revive concern about the sovereign-policy mix.

In credit, lighter projected investment-grade issuance will test whether record order attrition was a temporary response to calendar congestion or the start of a more durable repricing. Investors accepted $136 billion of supply over 2 weeks, but withdrew orders when issuers tightened too aggressively. The next deals will show whether a slower calendar restores borrowers’ pricing power or whether Treasury yields, AI capital demands and contingent liabilities have raised the minimum compensation required across the market.

section_summaries.section_title: Fiscal Promises and Policy Divergence Reshape Global Debt
section_summaries.summary: Indonesia proposed a 2.4%-of-GDP deficit target for next year, but revenue, subsidy and spending assumptions still face an execution test. The Philippines signaled less aggressive inflation restraint as growth weakened, while Australia and Japan retained near-term tightening risk. Kenya and Colombian companies regained selective market access as yields fell, though debt distress and fiscal constraints kept refinancing costs consequential.

The new week will test whether Iran-related measures and shipping risks sustain the oil-led Treasury reversal, whether the $16 billion 20-year auction attracts demand near historically high yields, and whether core PCE inflation confirms that moderation extends beyond energy-sensitive categories. Fed minutes, China activity data and several overseas policy and inflation releases provide additional tests of growth and tightening expectations.

overall_summary.headline: Oil Reverses Treasury Relief as Weak Consumer Data Softens Near-Term Fed Risk
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries reversed an early rally and closed with higher yields across the curve. The 2-year yield rose 2.8 basis points to 4.171%, the 10-year climbed 4.9 basis points to 4.693% and the 30-year added 4.6 basis points to 5.261%, while the 2s10s curve steepened 2.1 basis points to 52.2 basis points. The 10-year move was almost evenly divided between a 2.5-basis-point increase in the real yield and a 2.4-basis-point rise in breakeven inflation.

July retail sales fell 0.6% and preliminary August consumer sentiment dropped to 51, initially pushing the 2-year yield below 4.10% as traders reduced expectations for a September Fed increase. That relief faded after WTI rose 1.42% to $82.40 and Brent gained 1.67% to $88.52 on threatened additional US economic measures against Iran and the continued blockade of Iranian ports. The oil move raised the risk that energy’s favorable contribution to recent inflation data will prove temporary, while heavy Treasury and corporate financing needs kept pressure on longer maturities.

Credit remained available but became more price-sensitive. Investment-grade investors withdrew about 36% of initial orders during a heavy issuance week as borrowers tightened pricing, showing that large orderbooks were not firm at every spread.
overall_summary.summary: Weaker retail sales and sentiment initially reduced near-term Fed tightening wagers, but oil’s advance on threatened new US measures against Iran revived inflation risk and, alongside heavy financing needs, drove a broad Treasury reversal led by the long end.
